+"""RPF3 reader controls on synthetic archives: tree, encryption, DEFLATE, resources and malformed tables."""
+import struct
+import unittest
+import zlib
+
+from mcla_rpf import RSC5, Rpf3Archive, jenkins
+from test_aes_decrypt import AesEncryptor
+
+KEY = bytes(range(32))
+
+
+def deflate(data):
+    packer = zlib.compressobj(9, zlib.DEFLATED, -15)
+    return packer.compress(data) + packer.flush()
+
+
+def encrypt16(table, key):
+    aes = AesEncryptor(key)
+    for _ in range(16):
+        table = aes.ecb(table)
+    return table
+
+
+def rpf_fixture(tree, key=None):
+    """tree: {name: subtree-dict | ('loose', bytes) | ('deflate', bytes) | ('resource', type, bytes)}."""
+    entries, blobs = [None], []
+    queue = [(0, tree)]
+    while queue:
+        index, children = queue.pop(0)
+        first = len(entries)
+        names = sorted(children)
+        entries.extend([None] * len(names))
+        entries[index] = ('directory', 0 if index == 0 else entries[index][1], first, len(names))
+        for offset, name in enumerate(names):
+            child = children[name]
+            if isinstance(child, dict):
+                entries[first + offset] = ('directory', jenkins(name), None, None)
+                queue.append((first + offset, child))
+            else:
+                entries[first + offset] = ('file', jenkins(name), child)
+                blobs.append(first + offset)
+    toc = bytearray(16 * len(entries))
+    data, position = bytearray(), (0x800 + len(toc) + 0x7FF) & ~0x7FF
+    placed = {}
+    for index in blobs:
+        _, _, spec = entries[index]
+        stored = deflate(spec[1]) if spec[0] == 'deflate' else spec[-1]
+        placed[index] = position
+        data += stored + bytes((-len(stored)) % 0x800)
+        position += len(stored) + (-len(stored)) % 0x800
+    for index, entry in enumerate(entries):
+        if entry[0] == 'directory':
+            struct.pack_into('<IIII', toc, 16 * index, entry[1], 0, 0x80000000 | entry[2], entry[3])
+            continue
+        spec, at = entry[2], placed[index]
+        if spec[0] == 'resource':
+            struct.pack_into('<IIII', toc, 16 * index, entry[1], len(spec[2]), at | spec[1], 0xC0000000)
+        elif spec[0] == 'deflate':
+            struct.pack_into('<IIII', toc, 16 * index, entry[1], len(spec[1]), at, 0x40000000 | len(deflate(spec[1])))
+        else:
+            struct.pack_into('<IIII', toc, 16 * index, entry[1], len(spec[1]), at, len(spec[1]))
+    table = encrypt16(bytes(toc), key) if key else bytes(toc)
+    header = struct.pack('<4sIIIi', b'RPF3', len(table), len(entries), 0, -1 if key else 0)
+    image = bytearray(header + bytes(0x800 - len(header)) + table)
+    image += bytes((-len(image)) % 0x800)
+    image += data
+    return bytes(image)
+
+
+TREE = {'resources': {'vehicle': {'vp_test_car_01': {'body_lod_0.xrsc': ('resource', 63, RSC5 + b'\0\0\0\x3f model'),
+                                                     'vp_test_car_01.xct': ('resource', 50, RSC5 + b' tune')}},
+                      'notes.xml': ('deflate', b'<names>vp_test_car_01</names>' * 20)},
+        'readme.txt': ('loose', b'plain')}
+
+
+def opened(image, key=None):
+    return Rpf3Archive(lambda o, s: image[o:o + s], len(image), key)
+
+
+class Rpf3Tests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_jenkins_one_at_a_time_vectors(self):
+        self.assertEqual(jenkins('a'), 0xCA2E9442)
+        self.assertEqual(jenkins('VP_Test'), jenkins('vp_test'))
+
+    def test_reads_tree_payloads_and_encrypted_tables(self):
+        for key in (None, KEY):
+            archive = opened(rpf_fixture(TREE, key), key)
+            self.assertEqual(archive.encrypted, key is not None)
+            by_hash = {e['hash']: e for e in archive.entries}
+            notes = by_hash[jenkins('notes.xml')]
+            self.assertTrue(notes['compressed'])
+            self.assertEqual(archive.payload(notes), TREE['resources']['notes.xml'][1])
+            body = by_hash[jenkins('body_lod_0.xrsc')]
+            self.assertEqual((body['resource'], body['resource_type']), (True, 63))
+            self.assertEqual(archive.payload(body), archive.stored(body))
+            car = by_hash[jenkins('vp_test_car_01')]
+            self.assertEqual(body['parent'], car['index'])
+            self.assertEqual(archive.payload(by_hash[jenkins('readme.txt')]), b'plain')
+
+    def test_rejects_wrong_key_and_missing_key(self):
+        image = rpf_fixture(TREE, KEY)
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'needs the AES key'):
+            opened(image)
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'root is not a directory|outside|unreachable|two parents'):
+            opened(image, bytes(32))
+
+    def test_rejects_malformed_tables_and_payloads(self):
+        image = bytearray(rpf_fixture(TREE))
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'not an RPF3'):
+            opened(b'RPF2' + bytes(image[4:]))
+        orphan = bytearray(image)
+        struct.pack_into('<I', orphan, 0x800 + 12, 1)  # root claims only its first child
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'unreachable'):
+            opened(bytes(orphan))
+        twice = bytearray(image)
+        struct.pack_into('<I', twice, 0x800 + 16 + 8, 0x80000000 | 1)  # a child directory re-lists entry 1
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'children outside table|two parents'):
+            opened(bytes(twice))
+        archive = opened(bytes(image))
+        notes = next(e for e in archive.entries if e['hash'] == jenkins('notes.xml'))
+        outside = bytearray(image)
+        struct.pack_into('<I', outside, 0x800 + 16 * notes['index'] + 8, len(image))
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'file outside archive'):
+            opened(bytes(outside))
+        resized = bytearray(image)
+        struct.pack_into('<I', resized, 0x800 + 16 * notes['index'] + 4, notes['size'] + 1)
+        reopened = opened(bytes(resized))
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'deflate size mismatch'):
+            reopened.payload(reopened.entries[notes['index']])
+        body = next(e for e in archive.entries if e['hash'] == jenkins('body_lod_0.xrsc'))
+        stripped = bytearray(image)
+        stripped[body['offset']:body['offset'] + 4] = b'RSC7'
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'without RSC5'):
+            opened(bytes(stripped)).payload(body)
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    unittest.main()

+"""XDVDFS reader controls on synthetic images: tree walk, payload reads and malformed tables."""
+from pathlib import Path
+import struct
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+
+from xdvdfs import MAGIC, SECTOR, XdvdfsDisc
+
+
+def directory_table(records):
+    """records: (name, sector, size, attributes). A right-leaning tree: each record links the next."""
+    table, offsets = bytearray(), []
+    for name, *_ in records:
+        length = (14 + len(name) + 3) & ~3
+        if len(table) // SECTOR != (len(table) + length - 1) // SECTOR:
+            table += b'\xff' * (SECTOR - len(table) % SECTOR)
+        offsets.append(len(table))
+        table += bytes(length)
+    for i, (name, sector, size, attributes) in enumerate(records):
+        right = offsets[i + 1] // 4 if i + 1 < len(records) else 0
+        struct.pack_into('<HHIIBB', table, offsets[i], 0, right, sector, size, attributes, len(name))
+        table[offsets[i] + 14:offsets[i] + 14 + len(name)] = name.encode()
+    return bytes(table)
+
+
+def disc_fixture(files, directories=None):
+    """files: [(name, payload)] in the root; directories: {name: [(name, payload)]} one level deep."""
+    directories = directories or {}
+    sector = 34
+    blobs, root = {}, []
+
+    def place(data):
+        nonlocal sector
+        at = sector
+        blobs[at] = data
+        sector += max(1, (len(data) + SECTOR - 1) // SECTOR)
+        return at
+    for name, children in directories.items():
+        entries = [(child, place(data), len(data), 0x20) for child, data in children]
+        table = directory_table(entries)
+        root.append((name, place(table), len(table), 0x10))
+    root += [(name, place(data), len(data), 0x20) for name, data in files]
+    table = directory_table(root)
+    root_sector = place(table)
+    image = bytearray(sector * SECTOR)
+    descriptor = MAGIC + struct.pack('<IIQ', root_sector, len(table), 0)
+    image[32 * SECTOR:32 * SECTOR + len(descriptor)] = descriptor
+    image[32 * SECTOR + 0x7EC:33 * SECTOR] = MAGIC
+    for at, data in blobs.items():
+        image[at * SECTOR:at * SECTOR + len(data)] = data
+    return bytes(image)
+
+
+class XdvdfsTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def open(self, image):
+        temp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
+        self.addCleanup(temp.cleanup)
+        path = Path(temp.name) / 'disc.iso'
+        path.write_bytes(image)
+        disc = XdvdfsDisc(path)
+        self.addCleanup(disc.close)
+        return disc
+
+    def test_lists_tree_and_reads_payloads(self):
+        disc = self.open(disc_fixture([('default.xex', b'XEX2 body'), ('b.bin', b'')],
+                                      {'media': [('movie.bik', b'BIK' * 1000)]}))
+        self.assertEqual(disc.generation, 'plain')
+        paths = {e['path']: e for e in disc.entries}
+        self.assertEqual(sorted(paths), ['b.bin', 'default.xex', 'media/', 'media/movie.bik'])
+        self.assertEqual(disc.region(paths['media/movie.bik'])(0, 3000), b'BIK' * 1000)
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'outside XDVDFS file'):
+            disc.region(paths['default.xex'])(5, 5)
+
+    def test_rejects_malformed_images(self):
+        good = disc_fixture([('a.bin', b'abc')])
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'no XDVDFS volume descriptor'):
+            self.open(bytes(len(good)))
+        trailer = bytearray(good)
+        trailer[33 * SECTOR - 1] ^= 1
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'trailer mismatch'):
+            self.open(bytes(trailer))
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'truncated'):
+            self.open(good[:-1])
+        root = struct.unpack_from('<I', good, 32 * SECTOR + 20)[0] * SECTOR
+        cyclic = bytearray(disc_fixture([('a.bin', b'abc'), ('b.bin', b'def')]))
+        croot = struct.unpack_from('<I', cyclic, 32 * SECTOR + 20)[0] * SECTOR
+        second = struct.unpack_from('<H', cyclic, croot + 2)[0] * 4
+        struct.pack_into('<H', cyclic, croot + second + 2, second // 4)  # second record links itself
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'tree cycle'):
+            self.open(bytes(cyclic))
+        outside = bytearray(good)
+        struct.pack_into('<I', outside, root + 8, 10 ** 6)
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'file outside disc'):
+            self.open(bytes(outside))
+        unsafe = bytearray(good)
+        struct.pack_into('B', unsafe, root + 13, 2)
+        unsafe[root + 14:root + 16] = b'..'
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'unsafe XDVDFS name'):
+            self.open(bytes(unsafe))
+
+    def test_rejects_overlapping_extents(self):
+        image = bytearray(disc_fixture([('a.bin', b'a' * 3000), ('b.bin', b'b' * 10)]))
+        root = struct.unpack_from('<I', image, 32 * SECTOR + 20)[0] * SECTOR
+        second = struct.unpack_from('<H', image, root + 2)[0] * 4
+        first_sector = struct.unpack_from('<I', image, root + 4)[0]
+        struct.pack_into('<I', image, root + second + 4, first_sector + 1)
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'overlapping'):
+            self.open(bytes(image))
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    unittest.main()

+"""XEX2 loader controls on synthetic executables: basic packing, retail-key encryption and rejections."""
+import struct
+import unittest
+
+from aes_decrypt import AesDecryptor
+from test_aes_decrypt import AesEncryptor
+from xex2 import RETAIL_KEY, load_image
+
+SESSION = bytes(range(16, 32))
+
+
+def pe_image(body=b'', size=0x3000):
+    image = bytearray(size)
+    image[:2] = b'MZ'
+    struct.pack_into('<I', image, 0x3C, 0x80)
+    image[0x80:0x84] = b'PE\0\0'
+    image[0x100:0x100 + len(body)] = body
+    return bytes(image)
+
+
+def xex_fixture(image, encrypted=True, compression=1, zero_tail=0x1000):
+    """Basic packing: the image minus a zero tail is stored, then the tail is zero-filled."""
+    stored = image[:len(image) - zero_tail]
+    if image[len(stored):] != bytes(zero_tail):
+        raise ValueError('fixture tail is not zero')
+    blocks = [(len(stored), zero_tail)]
+    format_info = struct.pack('>IHH', 8 + 8 * len(blocks), 1 if encrypted else 0, compression)
+    format_info += b''.join(struct.pack('>II', d, z) for d, z in blocks)
+    security_at, format_at, pe_at = 0x40, 0x200, 0x400
+    header = bytearray(pe_at)
+    struct.pack_into('>4sIIIII', header, 0, b'XEX2', 1, pe_at, 0, security_at, 1)
+    struct.pack_into('>II', header, 24, 0x3FF, format_at)
+    struct.pack_into('>I', header, security_at + 4, len(image))
+    file_key = AesEncryptor(RETAIL_KEY).ecb(SESSION)  # decrypts back to SESSION under the retail key
+    header[security_at + 0x150:security_at + 0x160] = file_key if encrypted else bytes(16)
+    header[format_at:format_at + len(format_info)] = format_info
+    payload = stored + bytes((-len(stored)) % 16)
+    if encrypted:
+        payload = AesEncryptor(SESSION).cbc(payload)
+    return bytes(header) + payload
+
+
+class Xex2Tests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_session_key_derivation(self):
+        self.assertEqual(AesDecryptor(RETAIL_KEY).ecb(AesEncryptor(RETAIL_KEY).ecb(SESSION)), SESSION)
+
+    def test_loads_encrypted_and_plain_basic_images(self):
+        image = pe_image(b'archive key lives here')
+        for encrypted in (True, False):
+            loaded, facts = load_image(xex_fixture(image, encrypted))
+            self.assertEqual(loaded, image)
+            self.assertEqual(facts['encryption'], int(encrypted))
+            self.assertEqual(facts['blocks'], [[len(image) - 0x1000, 0x1000]])
+
+    def test_rejects_unsupported_and_corrupt_executables(self):
+        image = pe_image()
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'not an XEX2'):
+            load_image(b'XEX1' + xex_fixture(image)[4:])
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'only basic'):
+            load_image(xex_fixture(image, compression=2))
+        wrong_key = bytearray(xex_fixture(image))
+        wrong_key[0x40 + 0x150] ^= 1
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'not a PE'):
+            load_image(bytes(wrong_key))
+        resized = bytearray(xex_fixture(image))
+        struct.pack_into('>I', resized, 0x40 + 4, len(image) + 0x1000)
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'disagree with image size'):
+            load_image(bytes(resized))
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'shorter than its blocks'):
+            load_image(xex_fixture(image)[:0x400 + 0x100])
+        odd = pe_image(size=0x3000 + 8)  # stored bytes end mid AES block
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'shorter than its blocks'):
+            load_image(xex_fixture(odd)[:-8])
+        self.assertEqual(load_image(xex_fixture(odd))[0], odd)
+        no_pe = bytearray(image)
+        no_pe[0x80:0x84] = b'NE\0\0'
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'lacks a PE header'):
+            load_image(xex_fixture(bytes(no_pe)))
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    unittest.main()

+"""Read-only XDVDFS (Xbox/Xbox 360 game partition) directory reader.
+
+Layout readings, checked against the Midnight Club: Los Angeles disc: the game
+partition starts at a fixed image offset per disc generation; its volume
+descriptor is sector 32 of the partition and carries `MICROSOFT*XBOX*MEDIA` at
+both ends, then the root directory sector and size. A directory is a binary
+search tree of 4-byte-aligned records: left and right subtree offsets in dwords,
+start sector, size, attribute byte (0x10 = directory), name length and name.
+Records never cross a sector boundary; 0xFF bytes pad the rest of a sector.
+"""
+from pathlib import Path
+import struct
+
+SECTOR = 2048
+MAGIC = b'MICROSOFT*XBOX*MEDIA'
+# Game-partition offsets by disc generation (XGD2 first: the generation of this disc).
+PARTITIONS = (('XGD2', 0xFD90000), ('XGD3', 0x2080000), ('XGD1', 0x18300000), ('plain', 0))
+DIRECTORY = 0x10
+MAX_DIRECTORY = 64 * 1024 * 1024
+MAX_ENTRIES = 1_000_000
+
+
+def safe_component(name):
+    if (not name or name in ('.', '..') or len(name) > 255 or '/' in name or '\\' in name
+            or any(ord(c) < 32 or ord(c) > 126 for c in name)):
+        raise ValueError('unsafe XDVDFS name')
+    return name
+
+
+class XdvdfsDisc:
+    """Lists every file and directory; reads payloads by entry. Never writes."""
+
+    def __init__(self, path):
+        self.path = Path(path)
+        if self.path.is_symlink():
+            raise ValueError('linked disc input')
+        self.stream = self.path.open('rb')
+        self.size = self.path.stat().st_size
+        try:
+            if self.size % SECTOR:
+                raise ValueError('truncated disc image')
+            for generation, base in PARTITIONS:
+                if base + 33 * SECTOR > self.size:
+                    continue
+                descriptor = self.read_at(base + 32 * SECTOR, SECTOR)
+                if descriptor[:20] == MAGIC:
+                    if descriptor[0x7EC:0x800] != MAGIC:
+                        raise ValueError('XDVDFS descriptor trailer mismatch')
+                    break
+            else:
+                raise ValueError('no XDVDFS volume descriptor')
+            self.generation, self.partition = generation, base
+            root_sector, root_size = struct.unpack_from('<II', descriptor, 20)
+            self.root = {'sector': root_sector, 'size': root_size}
+            self.timestamp = struct.unpack_from('<Q', descriptor, 28)[0]
+            self.entries = []
+            self._walk(root_sector, root_size, '', set())
+            self.entries.sort(key=lambda e: e['path'])
+            files = sorted((e for e in self.entries if e['kind'] == 'file' and e['size']), key=lambda e: e['sector'])
+            for previous, current in zip(files, files[1:]):
+                if previous['sector'] * SECTOR + previous['size'] > current['sector'] * SECTOR:
+                    raise ValueError('overlapping XDVDFS file extents')
+        except Exception:
+            self.close()
+            raise
+
+    def close(self):
+        self.stream.close()
+
+    def read_at(self, offset, size):
+        if offset < 0 or size < 0 or offset + size > self.size:
+            raise ValueError('read outside disc')
+        self.stream.seek(offset)
+        data = self.stream.read(size)
+        if len(data) != size:
+            raise ValueError('truncated disc read')
+        return data
+
+    def offset(self, sector):
+        return self.partition + sector * SECTOR
+
+    def region(self, entry):
+        if entry['kind'] != 'file':
+            raise ValueError('not an XDVDFS file')
+        start, size = self.offset(entry['sector']), entry['size']
+
+        def read(offset, count):
+            if offset < 0 or count < 0 or offset + count > size:
+                raise ValueError('read outside XDVDFS file')
+            return self.read_at(start + offset, count)
+        return read
+
+    def _walk(self, sector, size, parent, seen):
+        if (sector, size) in seen:
+            raise ValueError('XDVDFS directory cycle')
+        if not 0 < size <= MAX_DIRECTORY or self.offset(sector) + size > self.size:
+            raise ValueError('XDVDFS directory outside disc')
+        seen.add((sector, size))
+        table = self.read_at(self.offset(sector), (size + SECTOR - 1) // SECTOR * SECTOR)[:size]
+        visited, names, stack = set(), set(), [0]
+        while stack:
+            at = stack.pop()
+            if at in visited:
+                raise ValueError('XDVDFS tree cycle')
+            visited.add(at)
+            if at + 14 > size or at // SECTOR != (at + 13) // SECTOR:
+                raise ValueError('XDVDFS record outside directory')
+            left, right, start, length, attributes, name_length = struct.unpack_from('<HHIIBB', table, at)
+            end = at + 14 + name_length
+            if not name_length or end > size or at // SECTOR != (end - 1) // SECTOR:
+                raise ValueError('XDVDFS name outside directory')
+            name = safe_component(table[at + 14:end].decode('ascii'))
+            if name.casefold() in names:
+                raise ValueError('duplicate XDVDFS name')
+            names.add(name.casefold())
+            path = parent + name
+            kind = 'directory' if attributes & DIRECTORY else 'file'
+            if kind == 'file' and length and self.offset(start) + length > self.size:
+                raise ValueError('XDVDFS file outside disc')
+            self.entries.append({'path': path + ('/' if kind == 'directory' else ''), 'kind': kind,
+                                 'sector': start, 'size': length, 'attributes': attributes})
+            if len(self.entries) > MAX_ENTRIES:
+                raise ValueError('XDVDFS entry limit')
+            if kind == 'directory' and length:
+                self._walk(start, length, path + '/', seen)
+            for child in (left, right):
+                if child:
+                    stack.append(child * 4)
